Query: When is repeat lumbar fusion indicated for symptomatic pseudoarthrosis?
Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level)

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months elapsed since the prior lumbar fusion
Daily pain of clinically significant intensity causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing)
Physical examination findings that are concordant with the reported symptoms

Less than clinically meaningful improvement despite BOTH a six‑week trial of prescription‑strength analgesics (including steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs) AND a six‑week provider‑directed exercise program (physical therapy, chiropractic, osteopathic or allopathic physician‑prescribed)
Post‑operative imaging performed at ≥6 months after the index fusion demonstrating pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s) (plain radiographs, CT or MRI) with findings concordant to symptoms
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)
Documentation of nicotine‑free status either as a never‑smoker or ≥6 weeks abstinence from all nicotine products verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine or saliva)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level > Symptomatic Pseudoarthrosis

Non-Indications: Less than six (6) months since the prior lumbar fusion
Pain or functional limitation that is mild/moderate and does not meet the threshold of clinically significant daily impairment
Absence of imaging evidence of pseudoarthrosis or discordance between imaging and symptoms
Failure to complete the required six‑week trial of both pharmacologic therapy and supervised exercise program
Active tobacco use without documented cessation and objective cotinine verification
Presence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Urgent/emergent indications that bypass the repeat‑fusion criteria (e.g., infection, fracture)
Important criteria & exceptions: Nicotine‑free status may be satisfied by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) with method‑specific normal cut‑offs (serum ≤ 20 ng/mL, urine ≤ 10 ng/mL, saliva ≤ 44 ng/mL) performed within six weeks prior to surgery

If intra‑operative findings reveal instability, imaging criteria may be waived per the “Actual Instability” exception, but the repeat‑fusion pseudoarthrosis pathway still requires the six‑month interval and other criteria
Conservative therapy must be documented as continuous for the full six‑week period; intermittent or shorter courses do not satisfy the requirement
Documentation required: Operative report of the index lumbar fusion (including level(s) fused and instrumentation used)
Post‑operative plain radiographs (flexion‑extension) and/or CT/MRI report dated ≥6 months post‑fusion demonstrating pseudoarthrosis (e.g., lack of bridging bone, hardware loosening)
Radiology report interpreting imaging and correlating findings with patient symptoms
Comprehensive physical examination note documenting neurologic and musculoskeletal findings consistent with pseudoarthrosis
Medication administration record showing at least six weeks of prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs with dosing details
Physical therapy (or chiropractic/osteopathic) progress notes confirming a supervised exercise program of at least six weeks with frequency and duration documented
Behavioral health evaluation confirming no unmanaged major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder
Objective cotinine test result (serum, urine, or saliva) with date, method, laboratory name, and values within normal range
Smoking cessation documentation (if former smoker) confirming ≥6 weeks abstinence
